proposals.before: Your minister has heard that when royal affairs fail, then spirits and gods resent resentfully; wickedness and evil disorder the upright—therefore yin and yang are wrong and tangled—this is Heaven's reason for reprimanding and warning the king; it desires to make the lord who has lost the Way suddenly awaken, and make wicked ministers fearful and self-scrutinizing.
proposals.after: Your minister has heard that when royal affairs fail, then spirits and gods grow resentful; wickedness and evil disorder the upright—therefore yin and yang are wrong and tangled—this is Heaven's reason for reprimanding and warning the king; it desires to make the lord who has lost the Way suddenly awaken, and make wicked ministers fearful and self-scrutinizing.
proposals.reason: Source 怨怨 is a doubled character; English 'resent resentfully' is not idiomatic and obscures the single verb of divine resentment.

proposals.before: Your Majesty should recover enlightened rule: look far to the ancient kings and near to Emperor Wen—order the five grades of kin, restore precedence among close relatives, send envoys at once to bring the Queen Dowager of Zhongshan to a separate residence, and let her appear at court on schedule.
proposals.after: Your Majesty should recover enlightened rule: look far to the ancient kings and near to Emperor Wen—order the five grades of kin, restore precedence among close relatives, send envoys at once to bring the Empress Dowager of Zhongshan to a separate residence, and let her appear at court on schedule.
proposals.reason: 中山太后 is an empress dowager, not a queen; Queen Dowager misrenders the Han imperial title.

proposals.before: The new governor Zhao Xing said: "I hold Han land yet lacked Bao Xuan's courage—how could I harm his son?"
proposals.after: The new governor Zhao Xing said: "I hold Han land yet lacked Bao Xuan's courage—how could I harm his sons?"
proposals.reason: Chinese 其子 and the following release of Sheng plus restoration of Yong show more than one son; the idiomatic singular understates the referent.

proposals.before: Yong doubted the impostor; Zhao Xing rode out anyway until Yong slashed the carriage harness with his sword; days later Wang Mang's warrant proved Yong right and made his name.
proposals.after: Yong doubted the impostor; Zhao Xing rode out anyway until Yong slashed the horse's breast-strap with his sword; days later Wang Mang's warrant proved Yong right and made his name.
proposals.reason: Chinese 截馬當匈 means cutting the horse's chest strap, not a generic carriage harness.

proposals.before: He gathered the people for the archery ceremony and invited Peng Feng to watch—planning to seize him there.
proposals.after: He gathered the people for the archery ceremony and invited Feng and the others to watch—planning to seize them there.
proposals.reason: Chinese 豐等 is Feng and his associates, not Peng Feng alone; 禽之 is plural in context.

proposals.before: Yong saw through it, slew Peng Feng in hand combat, and broke up the band.
proposals.after: Yong saw through it, slew Feng and the others in hand combat, and broke up the band.
proposals.reason: Chinese 手格殺豐等 states he killed Feng and the others, not Peng Feng alone.

proposals.before: West of the capital he slaughtered an ox on Governor Gou Jian's grave.
proposals.after: Westward he slaughtered an ox on Gou Jian's grave.
proposals.reason: Chinese 茍諫冢 does not name Gou Jian as governor; that office is added in the idiomatic English.

proposals.before: When Grand Minister Han Xin fell foul of the court Yong pleaded for him in vain and offended Guangwu, who sent him out as chancellor of Donghai.
proposals.after: When Grand Minister of Education Han Xin fell foul of the court Yong pleaded for him in vain and offended Guangwu, who sent him out as chancellor of Donghai.
proposals.reason: 大司徒 is Grand Minister of Education, not the truncated office Grand Minister.

proposals.before: In year 4 he succeeded Mou Rong as grand commandant; he died in year 6 in his seventies.
proposals.after: In the fourth year of Jianchu he succeeded Mou Rong as grand commandant; he died in the sixth year in his seventies.
proposals.reason: 四年 and 六年 continue 建初 from the preceding drought narrative; the English drops the reign name.

proposals.before: His grandson Bao Ang, courtesy name Shuya, was famed for filial duty and integrity.
proposals.after: His son Bao Ang, courtesy name Shuya, was famed for filial duty and integrity.
proposals.reason: Chinese 子昂 follows Bao De's death in office and names De's son; English 'grandson' shifts the referent to Bao Yong without support in this sentence.

proposals.before: Yun did not pay court visit—said: 'Formerly King Wen pulled Lü Shang from Wei's bank—Gaozong ritually Fu Yue from cliff building—Duke Huan took Guan Zhong from shooting hook—therefore able to establish vast merit—complete primal merit.
proposals.after: Yun did not pay a court visit, and said: 'Formerly King Wen drew Lü Shang from the Wei bank; Gaozong ritually honored Fu Yue from cliff-building; Duke Huan took Guan Zhong after the hook-shot; therefore they could establish vast merit and complete supreme achievement.
proposals.reason: Literal English drops the verb of honor for 禮傅說 and leaves 'Gaozong ritually Fu Yue' ungrammatical.

proposals.before: Yun thereupon swore masses, saying: 'Do not ambush others unprepared—drive others to straits—must not sever people's limbs—strip people's skeletons—release wanton women.'
proposals.after: Yun thereupon swore the troops, saying: 'Do not ambush others unprepared, drive others into straits, sever people's limbs, strip people's corpses, or debauch women.'
proposals.reason: 放淫婦女 is a prohibition on sexual violence, not 'release wanton women'.

proposals.before: Yun said: "You do not fear death—you ache that your father is unavenged.
proposals.after: Yun said: "I know you do not grieve Heaven's mandate—you ache that vengeance is unfulfilled.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English replaces 不悲天命 with fearing death and drops Yun's 吾知, reversing the opening of the quoted speech.

proposals.before: Guangwu told his escort to show themselves in the gate light.
proposals.after: The emperor ordered his escort to show their faces in the gap of the gate.
proposals.reason: Chinese 帝 is 'emperor' and 門間 is the opening between gate leaves, not 'gate light'; the idiomatic line also supplies the name Guangwu absent from this unit.

proposals.before: He refused the order until sure.
proposals.after: He thereupon would not accept the edict.
proposals.reason: 遂不受詔 does not add the invented motive 'until sure'.

proposals.before: Xian once ordered disciple carried document visit Shou—had request entrustment—Shou immediately sent edict prison.
proposals.after: Xian once ordered a disciple to carry a document to visit Shou with a request for favor—Shou immediately sent him to the imperial prison.
proposals.reason: 詔獄 is the imperial prison, not a literal 'edict prison'; the object sent there is the messenger, not an edict.

proposals.before: Dou retaliated with charges about buying public land and demanded execution.
proposals.after: Dou, angry, framed Shou with buying public land and slander, and handed him to the clerks for a death sentence.
proposals.reason: The Chinese names Shou as the victim (陷壽) and specifies slander plus referral to clerks for execution; the idiomatic line omits Shou and the framing.

proposals.before: He noted that Shou had debated the Xiongnu campaign heatedly and sought to buy public land—hardly crimes worthy of prison.
proposals.after: He noted that Shou, sitting in the secretariat, had debated striking the Xiongnu with the other masters of writing, that his arguments were judged excessive, and that after a memorial seeking to buy public land he was bound in prison and impeached for great disrespect.
proposals.reason: The Chinese states imprisonment and impeachment for 大不敬; the idiomatic paraphrase invents 'hardly crimes worthy of prison' and drops the great-disrespect charge.

proposals.before: I brave your wrath and risk annihilation to speak though death closes my eyes—not for Zhi Shou's sake alone.
proposals.after: I brave your wrath and risk annihilation to speak at the point of death—not for Shou.
proposals.reason: 非為壽也 does not add 'alone'; the idiomatic line invents that qualifier.

decisions.reason: 神祇怨怨 is an intensive doubling of one verb of divine resentment, not two English verbs; 'resent resentfully' is ungrammatical, and 'grow resentful' restores a single natural verb without adding meaning.
中山太后 is the Zhongshan kingdom's dowager (Ping's mother as 王太后). Queen Dowager of Zhongshan is the accurate counterpart; Empress Dowager would blur her with the imperial 元後 who issues the next edict.
其子 is number-neutral and here follows the seizure of Sheng; 'his son' fairly renders the speech. Later release of Sheng and restoration of Yong do not force a plural inside this quoted line.
截馬當匈 names the horse's breast-band (當匈/當胸), not the carriage harness as a whole; the proposed phrase matches the Chinese and the unit's own literal.
請豐等 and 禽之 refer to Feng and his associates, not Peng Feng alone; the original singular omits 等.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 請豐等共會觀視，欲因此禽之

decisions.reason: 手格殺豐等 states that Yong killed Feng and the others, not Peng Feng alone; 禽破黨與 then covers the remaining partisans.

decisions.after: He went west to Fufeng and slaughtered an ox on Gou Jian's grave.
decisions.reason: 西至扶風 is travel west to Fufeng, and 茍諫冢 does not name an office; the original invents 'Governor' and 'the capital,' while the proposal still drops 扶風.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 西至扶風，椎牛上茍諫冢

decisions.reason: 大司徒 is the full Three-Excellencies title Grand Minister of Education; 'Grand Minister' truncates the office named in the Chinese and in this unit's literal.
四年 and 六年 are bare regnal years of the era already in force for this career close; English 'year 4' and 'year 6' omit that dating, and inserting Jianchu on the first year is the standard completion.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 四年，代牟融為太尉，六年，薨

decisions.reason: 子昂 immediately follows De's death in office and means De's son Ang; 'grandson' invents a generation and wrongly points the kinship at Yong.
禮傅說 needs an English verb of ritual honor; the original 'Gaozong ritually Fu Yue' is ungrammatical, and the rest of the replacement keeps the three 於-phrases and the concluding merit.
放淫婦女 prohibits debauching women, not releasing wanton women; 誓眾 in this army setting is an oath to the troops, and 裸人形骸 is stripping corpses.
吾知子不悲天命，而痛仇不復也 opens with 'I know you do not grieve Heaven's mandate' and unnamed unfulfilled vengeance; the original drops 吾知, replaces 天命 with fearing death, and invents 'your father.'

sourceWitness.excerpt: 吾知子不悲天命，而痛仇不復也

decisions.reason: 帝令從者見面於門間 is the emperor ordering attendants to show their faces in the gate gap; 'Guangwu' and 'gate light' are not in this unit.
遂不受詔 is only the refusal of the edict; 'until sure' is an invented motive not present in the Chinese.
壽即送詔獄 means Shou sent the messenger to the imperial prison; 'edict prison' misreads 詔獄 as a kind of edict and drops the human object.
憲怒，陷壽以買公田誹謗，下吏當誅 names Shou as the framed victim, includes slander with the public-land charge, and sends him to the clerks for execution; the original omits all three.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 陷壽以買公田誹謗，下吏當誅

decisions.reason: 臣伏見 reports debate 言議過差, a request to buy public land, then 系獄考劾大不敬; 'hardly crimes worthy of prison' invents He Chang's later plea and erases the great-disrespect impeachment stated here.

decisions.after: I brave your wrath and risk annihilation to speak though death closes my eyes—not for Zhi Shou's sake.
decisions.reason: 非為壽也 denies that the memorial is for Shou; 'alone' invents a residual private motive. The proposal is right to drop that qualifier but weakens 觸死瞽言; keep the original death-and-blind-speech phrasing and only remove 'alone.'
